examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Quine–McCluskey groups minterms by one-bit counts and combines terms differing in exactly one specified bit. A dash indicates an eliminated variable. Only terms with the same dash positions can be combined in later rounds. Uncombined terms become prime implicants. A prime-implicant chart then solves the cover problem; finding all primes is not the same as selecting a minimum cover.

**Key relationship:** Combine 010 and 011 → 01−; combine only terms with matching dash positions

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Combine compatible one-bit differences.
2. Mark combined terms and collect uncombined primes.
3. Cover required minterms, starting with essential primes.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Group minterms by number of 1 bits and combine terms differing in exactly one non-dash position. Repeat until no further valid combination exists. Uncombined terms are prime implicants. A prime-implicant chart selects a cover; generating prime implicants alone does not complete minimum-cover selection.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A four-variable implicant has pattern 1−0−. How many minterms does it cover?

**Answer: 4.** Two dash positions independently take either bit, so there are 2²=4 minterms: 1000,1001,1100,1101. The retained literals are A and ¬C.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Only terms with identical dash positions can be combined at the next stage. A non-dash bit difference must be exactly one, not two.

Two dashed terms combine only when their dash positions match and one remaining bit differs.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Combining binary terms 010 and 011 gives:

- **A.** −10
- **B.** 111
- **C.** 01−
- **D.** 0−0

**Answer: C.** Only the last bit differs, so it becomes a dash while the common first two bits remain.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose correct statements.

- **A.** Prime implicants may cover don't-cares
- **B.** All prime implicants must appear in every minimum cover
- **C.** Essential implicants cover a uniquely covered required minterm
- **D.** A chart is needed after prime generation to select a cover

**Answer: A, C, D.** Optional primes can be redundant. A prime is essential only when a required minterm has no alternative coverage.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Terms 000,001,010,011 combine fully. How many variables remain in the final implicant?



**Answer: 1.** Both the second and third bits vary. The first remains zero, giving 0−− and one literal.
